messages:
mike: heads up — we need a short plan for SSH access and audit for the upcoming private deploys. questions: jumpbox vs ssh-proxy vs cert-based bastion, where KMS signs certs, and how to get audit logs to siem without leaking customer subnets

alice: +1. prefer cert-based short-lived certs if feasible. avoid long-lived keys.

sre-jen: can we scope this: is this for on-prem racks or vpc-only? network constraints change options.

mike: both. vpc + on-prem. goal: no direct admin ssh into prod hosts, centralized proxy, full command-level audit (who ran what), and key material never stored plaintext.

carla: for on-prem we use a bastion VM today. options: 1) sshd jump host with forced-command + auditd -> logs to syslog -> forward to SIEM 2) ssh-cert flow: CA signs short certs via KMS-backed CA 3) SSH proxy (sshd ProxyCommand /sft) + session recording (tsh/teleport)

paul: teleport style gives session recording + RBAC out of box. but we need to evaluate offline air-gapped installs (some customers disallow outbound).

mike: tradeoffs: teleport nice but heavier. cert-based ssh is lighter but we need a CA signer (KMS integration). do we have a pattern to issue certificates from customer-managed KMS?

alice: we can run a small signing service inside the private control plane. signing key stored in HSM/KMS. service issues certs after OIDC/SCIM + RBAC check. short TTL (5-15m). signing operations require quorum of svc accounts.

carla: airflow: user requests -> an auth svc verifies identity -> mint cert -> client gets cert. must log: requestor, reason, IP, cert serial. ship logs to SIEM. if air-gapped, logs to local ELK with secure collection pipe.

sre-jen: implementation hints: ssh certificate options — principal includes roles. sshd config:
```
TrustedUserCAKeys /etc/ssh/ca.pub
AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand /usr/local/bin/principals.sh
```
PrincipalsCommand should map cert principals to local roles and enforce sudoers.

mike: question on KMS: do we want direct KMS sign API calls from signing svc, or rotate a signing key into the service via ephemeral credentials?

alice: use KMS sign API + key policy to restrict signer. For on-prem airgap where KMS can't be reached, use a hardware HSM on-site or a sealed signing key in an HSM appliance. Key material must never be in plain on disk.

paul: audit logs: need command-level capture. sshd's internal logging isn't enough. prefer process-level recording (script / auditd + tlog) or Teleport's session slices. minimal event set: session start/stop, executed commands, file transfers, SUDO events.

carla: sample audit line we'd like in SIEM:
```
{"ts":"2024-11-21T13:02:12Z","user":"alice","target":"node-42","action":"ssh-cert-session-start","cert_serial":"c-9876","role":"infra-admin","src_ip":"1.2.3.4"}
```
Make sure fields are structured for queries.

sre-jen: network isolation: jumpbox must only have outbound to logging endpoint and KMS (if allowed). use egress whitelist + VPC endpoints for KMS. no general internet egress. enforce with netpol / iptables on on-prem.

mike: RBAC change — we want to add a new group 'private-deploy-admins' with scoped perms. any blockers for granting the cert mint permission to that group?

alice: need to update auth svc to check group membership from SCIM/IdP. Also record any changes to group membership in audit logs. add approval flow for membership changes.

devsecops-bot: POLICY_CHANGE: RBAC group 'private-deploy-admins' created in audit-trail. See runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/ssh-access

paul: vuln triage: there's an sshd CVE (hypothetical CVE-2024-xxxx) that affects legacy algorithms. can we force config to only allow modern algorithms and reject old ciphers?

carla: yes, update sshd_config to:
```
Ciphers chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com
KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256
HostKeyAlgorithms rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256,ssh-ed25519
```
Also block password auth and set PermitRootLogin no.

sre-jen: deploy those via config management. schedule a canary rollout to a non-prod group then prod. create a preflight check for connectivity (some embedded devices might still use old algos).

mike: incident response: if signing svc is compromised, we need an emergency rotate + revoke plan. plan sketch: 1) revoke CA (generate CRL) 2) publish revocation info to nodes (update /etc/trusted-ca, force short cert reissue) 3) disable signing endpoints 4) full audit + forensics

alice: also publish a key rotation token to on-prem HSMs. for CRL: since SSH certs don't use CRLs well, prefer cert short TTL + publish a 'quarantine' list and block principals via sshd AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand lookup.

paul: add automation to push temporary host-level bannings to iptables for cert serials/principals flagged.

carla: for air-gapped, rotation includes physically sealing new key into HSM and running a signed attestation procedure. document chain-of-custody.

mike: next steps — create a short RFC + checklist. items: KMS signer design, signing svc auth flow, logging schema, session recording options per customer profile (connected vs air-gapped), RBAC group lifecycle, revocation runbook. volunteer owners?

alice: I'll own signing svc design + KMS integration.

sre-jen: I'll own network egress rules + sshd hardening rollout.

carla: I'll draft the audit schema + SIEM dashboards.

mike: thanks. I'll draft the RFC and collect runbook bits. ping me for a 30m sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:

devsecops-bot: MEETING_CREATED: Private-deploy SSH sync scheduled 2024-11-22 16:00 UTC. Calendar invite sent.
